prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Seek further information from owners/occupiers.
3. Analyse the inspection records; they may be difficult to understand and taken out of context.
4. Look at the 'big picture': the building as a whole.
5. Never rely on individual views of the building, as you might miss individual defects that are evident only in the context of the whole picture.
6. Review whether fire-safety issues arise from the design of the building or non-compliance with plans/test results of any samples. Where plans are missing, check the structure of the building from known drawings; e.g., adopt originally available specifications to rectify inconsistencies and problems.
7. Repeatedly review all the survey and background information to ensure that you understand the design of the building and its impact on fire safety. # Identify issues from fire-safety, routine maintenance, building control and regulatory records
